Question:
Is CN-TFE's oil pressure switch within the limit of AD 2013-11-11, according to its records?

Source: FLEET-2026-10, section 
CN-TFA Engine oil pressure switch 83278  2024-02-14 7210.4 3,000 h AD 2013-11-11
CN-TFB Engine oil pressure switch 83278  2023-05-09 5880 3,000 h AD 2013-11-11
CN-TFC Engine oil pressure switch 83278  2022-11-21 3350.7 3,000 h Procedures manual 3.2
CN-TFD Engine oil pressure switch 83278  2025-03-03 9940.2 3,000 h AD 2013-11-11
CN-TFE Engine oil pressure switch 83278  2021-08-30 10560.2 3,000 h AD 2013-11-11
CN-TFF Engine oil pressure switch 83278  2022-07-18 2410.5 3,000 h Procedures manual 3.2
CN-TFA ELT battery 452-6505  2021-01-19 4755.3 6 years ELT manufacturer
CN-TFE ELT battery 452-6505  2020-11-25 9810 6 years ELT manufacturer

Replaced engine oil pressure switch with new, zero-time switch P/N 83278, per AD 2013-11-11 paragraph (g)(6).
Ground run: oil pressure indication normal, no leaks. AD compliance record updated. Torque per maintenance manual. Wrench T-022.

Replaced engine oil pressure switch with new, zero-time switch P/N 83278, per AD 2013-11-11.
Removed switch P/N 83278 at 2,951.3 hours since installation.
Ground run: oil pressure indication normal, no leaks. Torque per maintenance manual. Wrench T-037.

Source: WO-SCAN, section Work
Replaced engine oil pressure switch with new, zero-time switch P/N 83278, per AD 2013-11-11 paragraph (g)(6) and Cessna Service Bulletin SB 07-79-01.
Removed switch P/N 83278 at 3,000.4 hours since installation. Ground run: oil pressure indication normal, no leaks.
Torque per maintenance manual. Wrench T-014.
Performed by: Y. Alaoui
Approved for return to service: A.Tazi alaouí
tazi

Source: PROC-R7, section 3
3.1 Tracking. Time-controlled parts are listed in the fleet register, sheet Time-controlled parts, with the airframe hours at installation. The hours used on a part are the airframe's current total time minus the airframe hours at installation.
3.2 Engine oil pressure switch. AD 2013-11-11 limits the engine oil pressure switch, P/N 83278, to 3,000 hours time-in-service on the airplanes within its applicability. Anfa applies the same 3,000-hour limit to every Cessna 172R and 172S it maintains, including those outside the directive's serial number ranges. Plan the replacement when a switch reaches 2,900 hours. Keep two switches in stock.
3.3 When the records disagree. If the fleet register and a work order or logbook give different hours for the same installation, use the lower airframe hours at installation until the quality manager has resolved the difference. Never use the figure that gives the part more time.

- Part: Engine oil pressure switch P/N 83278
- Date installed: 2021-08-30
- Airframe hours at installation: 10560.2
- Limit: 3,000 hours
- Reference: AD 2013-11-11

According to PROC-R7 section 3.2, AD 2013-11-11 limits the engine oil pressure switch P/N 83278 to 3,000 hours time-in-service. Anfa applies the same 3,000-hour limit to every Cessna 172R and 172S.

Section 3.1 says: "The hours used on a part are the airframe's current total time minus the airframe hours at installation."

However, I don't have the current airframe total time for CN-TFE. The fleet register shows the airframe hours at installation (10560.2), but not the current airframe hours.

The work orders show replacements for other aircraft (CN-TFA, CN-TFD, etc.) but not for CN-TFE specifically. The WO-SCAN entries mention replacements but don't specify which aircraft they're for (though one mentions "Replaced engine oil pressure switch with new, zero-time switch P/N 83278, per AD 2013-11-11 paragraph (g)(6)" and another mentions "Removed switch P/N 83278 at 3,000.4 hours since installation").

WO-2025-0095 mentions "Removed switch P/N 83278 at 2,951.3 hours since installation" but doesn't specify the aircraft.

Since I don't have the current airframe hours for CN-TFE, I cannot calculate the current hours on the switch (current airframe hours - 10560.2). Without that calculation, I cannot determine if it's within the 3,000-hour limit.

The fleet register is dated FLEET-2026-10 (suggesting October 2026), and the switch was installed on 2021-08-30 at 10560.2 airframe hours. But without knowing the current airframe hours as of the record date or now, I can't determine the time-in-service.

Therefore, the passages don't establish an answer.
